title: Adding and Subtracting Within 1,000
seo_title: Grade 2 Adding and Subtracting Within 1,000 Worksheets (TEKS 2.4C)
standard_text: 2.4C solve one-step and multi-step word problems involving addition and subtraction within 1,000 using a variety of strategies based on place value, including algorithms
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.4C: add and subtract within 1,000 with mental math, base-ten blocks, regrouping and open number lines. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the places and start with the ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Line up the ones, tens and hundreds.
  • Add or subtract one place at a time, starting with the ones.
  • Regroup when a place has 10 or more (adding) or not enough (subtracting).
  • Use an open number line to jump by hundreds, tens and ones.

Examples

Example

356 + 278

6 + 8 = 14: regroup

5 + 7 + 1 = 13: regroup

3 + 2 + 1 = 6

Answer: 634

Example

503 − 167

Regroup across the 0

13 − 7, 9 − 6, 4 − 1

Answer: 336

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to regroup14 ones = 1 ten and 4 ones.
Regrouping across a zero wrongly503 is 4 hundreds, 9 tens, 13 ones.
Adding the wrong placesLine up the digits by place value.

faq.a: Solve one-step and multi-step word problems involving addition and subtraction within 1,000 using a variety of strategies based on place value, including algorithms.

faq.q: What is an open number line?
faq.a: A line with no marks where you draw your own jumps.

faq.q: How can I check my answer?
faq.a: Estimate first, or add back to check a subtraction.

sets.title: Mental math with tens and hundreds

items.e: Adding 100 changes only the hundreds digit. It goes from 5 to 6. 509 + 100 = 609.
Subtracting 100 changes only the hundreds digit. It goes from 4 to 3. 405 − 100 = 305.
Adding 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 4 to 5. The hundreds and ones stay the same. 345 + 10 = 355.
Subtracting 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 5 to 4. 853 − 10 = 843.
Subtracting 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 8 to 7. 486 − 10 = 476.
Adding 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 6 to 7. The hundreds and ones stay the same. 768 + 10 = 778.
Adding 100 changes only the hundreds digit. It goes from 8 to 9. 836 + 100 = 936.
Subtracting 100 changes only the hundreds digit. It goes from 7 to 6. 718 − 100 = 618.
Adding 100 changes only the hundreds digit. It goes from 2 to 3. 274 + 100 = 374.
Adding 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 1 to 2. The hundreds and ones stay the same. 512 + 10 = 522.
Adding 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 3 to 4. The hundreds and ones stay the same. 230 + 10 = 240.
Subtracting 10 changes only the tens digit. It goes from 2 to 1. 627 − 10 = 617.
10 more is 1 more rod. 4 tens become 5 tens: 253. The flats and cubes stay the same.
100 less is 1 flat fewer. 3 hundreds become 2 hundreds: 215. The rod and cubes stay the same.
395 has 9 tens. 1 more ten makes 10 tens, and 10 tens make 1 hundred. So 3 hundreds become 4 hundreds, and the tens become 0. 395 + 10 = 405.
692 has 9 tens. 1 more ten makes 10 tens, and 10 tens make 1 hundred. So 6 hundreds become 7 hundreds, and the tens become 0. 692 + 10 = 702.
402 has 0 tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 3 hundreds and 10 tens. Take away 1 ten: 9 tens are left. 402 − 10 = 392. The hundreds go down too.
805 has 0 tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 7 hundreds and 10 tens. Take away 1 ten: 9 tens are left. 805 − 10 = 795. The hundreds go down too.
490 + 10 = 500. 49 tens and 1 more ten make 50 tens, which is 5 hundreds.

items.q: Count back by 100s: 850, 750, 650, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 less. 650 − 100 = 550. Only the hundreds digit changes.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 3 + 3 = 6 hundreds. Rods: 1 + 1 = 2 tens. Cubes: 4 + 4 = 8 ones. That is 628.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 3 + 2 = 5 hundreds. Rods: 0 + 2 = 2 tens. Cubes: 3 + 3 = 6 ones. That is 526.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 3 + 2 = 5 hundreds. Rods: 4 + 2 = 6 tens. Cubes: 2 + 6 = 8 ones. That is 568.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 1 + 1 = 2 hundreds. Rods: 0 + 4 = 4 tens. Cubes: 4 + 4 = 8 ones. That is 248.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 1 + 1 = 2 hundreds. Rods: 4 + 2 = 6 tens. Cubes: 1 + 2 = 3 ones. That is 263.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 1 + 3 = 4 hundreds. Rods: 0 + 5 = 5 tens. Cubes: 3 + 4 = 7 ones. That is 457.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 3 + 3 = 6 hundreds. Rods: 4 + 0 = 4 tens. Cubes: 1 + 3 = 4 ones. That is 644.
Count the same kinds together. Flats: 2 + 2 = 4 hundreds. Rods: 6 + 3 = 9 tens. Cubes: 3 + 5 = 8 ones. That is 498.
3 hundreds + 4 hundreds = 7 hundreds. 300 + 400 = 700.
300 is 3 hundreds. Add them to the hundreds: 2 + 3 = 5 hundreds. 250 + 300 = 550.
600 is 6 hundreds and 40 is 4 tens. They are different places, so do not add 6 + 4. 600 + 40 = 640.
70 is 7 tens. 2 tens + 7 tens = 9 tens. 120 + 70 = 190.

items.e: 32 is 3 tens and 2 ones. It has no hundreds. Tens: 2 + 3 = 5. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Answer: 457.
54 is 5 tens and 4 ones. It has no hundreds. Tens: 1 + 5 = 6. Ones: 3 + 4 = 7. Answer: 467.
26 is 2 tens and 6 ones. It has no hundreds. Tens: 4 + 2 = 6. Ones: 2 + 6 = 8. Answer: 368.
47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. It has no hundreds. Tens: 5 + 4 = 9. Ones: 1 + 7 = 8. Answer: 398.

items.q: You have 3 hundreds, 14 tens, 2 ones. What number is that?
items.e: 14 tens is 1 hundred and 4 tens. So there are 4 hundreds, 4 tens and 2 ones: 442.

items.q: You have 5 hundreds, 2 tens, 13 ones. What number is that?
items.e: 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. So there are 5 hundreds, 3 tens and 3 ones: 533.

items.q: You have 2 hundreds, 11 tens, 6 ones. What number is that?
items.e: 11 tens is 1 hundred and 1 ten. So there are 3 hundreds, 1 ten and 6 ones: 316.
There are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. Ones: 5 + 5 = 10 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 0 ones. Tens: 4 + 4 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 3 + 2 = 5. Answer: 590.
There are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. Ones: 5 + 5 = 10 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 0 ones. Tens: 0 + 1 + 1 = 2. Hundreds: 3 + 3 = 6. Answer: 620.
There are 12 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. Ones: 7 + 5 = 12 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 2 ones. Tens: 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 2 + 3 = 5. Answer: 572.
There are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. Ones: 6 + 4 = 10 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 0 ones. Tens: 6 + 1 + 1 = 8. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 380.

items.q: What is 117 + 114? Use the blocks.
items.e: There are 11 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. Ones: 7 + 4 = 11 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 1 one. Tens: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 231.
There are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. Ones: 3 + 7 = 10 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 0 ones. Tens: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 2 + 2 = 4. Answer: 470.
Ones: 6 + 5 = 11 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 1 one. Tens: 2 + 6 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 2 + 2 = 4. Answer: 491.
Ones: 7 + 4 = 11 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 1 one. Tens: 6 + 1 + 1 = 8. Hundreds: 4 + 4 = 8. Answer: 881.
Ones: 7 + 7 = 14 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 4 ones. Tens: 5 + 0 + 1 = 6. Hundreds: 3 + 2 = 5. Answer: 564.
Hundreds: 200 + 100 = 300. Tens: 30 + 80 = 110. Ones: 2 + 3 = 5. 300 + 110 + 5 = 415. (11 tens make 1 hundred and 1 ten.)
Hundreds: 300 + 400 = 700. Tens: 80 + 50 = 130. Ones: 3 + 5 = 8. 700 + 130 + 8 = 838. (13 tens make 1 hundred and 3 tens.)
Hundreds: 300 + 400 = 700. Tens: 80 + 40 = 120. Ones: 4 + 2 = 6. 700 + 120 + 6 = 826. (12 tens make 1 hundred and 2 tens.)
Hundreds: 300 + 300 = 600. Tens: 70 + 60 = 130. Ones: 4 + 5 = 9. 600 + 130 + 9 = 739. (13 tens make 1 hundred and 3 tens.)
Hundreds: 200 + 100 = 300. Tens: 70 + 90 = 160. Ones: 4 + 1 = 5. 300 + 160 + 5 = 465. (16 tens make 1 hundred and 6 tens.)

items.q: Make a hundred first. What is 298 + 145?
items.e: Take 2 from 145 to make 298 + 2 = 300. Now add the rest: 300 + 143 = 443.

items.q: Make a hundred first. What is 399 + 226?
items.e: Take 1 from 226 to make 399 + 1 = 400. Now add the rest: 400 + 225 = 625.
Count the blocks that are not crossed out. Flats: 2 − 1 = 1. Rods: 6 − 4 = 2. Cubes: 8 − 4 = 4. 268 − 144 = 124.
Count the blocks that are not crossed out. Flats: 4 − 2 = 2. Rods: 4 − 3 = 1. Cubes: 6 − 3 = 3. 446 − 233 = 213.
Count the blocks that are not crossed out. Flats: 4 − 1 = 3. Rods: 2 − 1 = 1. Cubes: 4 − 2 = 2. 424 − 112 = 312.
Count the blocks that are not crossed out. Flats: 2 − 1 = 1. Rods: 4 − 1 = 3. Cubes: 7 − 1 = 6. 247 − 111 = 136.

items.q: The blocks show 327. The crossed-out blocks are 115. What is 327 − 115?
items.e: Count the blocks that are not crossed out. Flats: 3 − 1 = 2. Rods: 2 − 1 = 1. Cubes: 7 − 5 = 2. 327 − 115 = 212.
Trade 1 ten for 10 ones. 5 tens become 4 tens, and 2 ones become 12 ones. It is still 452.
Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens. 6 hundreds become 5 hundreds, and 1 ten becomes 11 tens. It is still 615.
503 has 0 tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 4 hundreds and 10 tens. It is still 503.
Ones: 2 − 8? Not enough ones. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. Hundreds: 5 − 4 = 1. Answer: 134. Check: 134 + 418 = 552.
Ones: 0 − 6? Not enough ones. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 5 − 4 = 1. Hundreds: 7 − 5 = 2. Answer: 214. Check: 214 + 546 = 760.
Ones: 2 − 9? Not enough ones. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 9 = 3. Tens: 2 − 2 = 0. Hundreds: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 303. Check: 303 + 129 = 432.
Ones: 5 − 9? Not enough ones. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 15 − 9 = 6. Tens: 8 − 6 = 2. Hundreds: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 226. Check: 226 + 369 = 595.
Ones: 8 − 8 = 0. Tens: 1 − 7? Not enough tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 11 − 7 = 4. Hundreds: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 440. Check: 440 + 278 = 718.
Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. Tens: 2 − 4? Not enough tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 12 − 4 = 8. Hundreds: 7 − 6 = 1. Answer: 184. Check: 184 + 643 = 827.
Ones: 8 − 2 = 6. Tens: 5 − 8? Not enough tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 15 − 8 = 7. Hundreds: 7 − 5 = 2. Answer: 276. Check: 276 + 582 = 858.
Ones: 3 − 8? Not enough ones, and there are 0 tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens. Then trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 9 − 2 = 7. Hundreds: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 375.
Ones: 2 − 6? Not enough ones, and there are 0 tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens. Then trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 6 = 6. Tens: 9 − 5 = 4. Hundreds: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 246.

items.q: Mateo says 534 − 218 = 316. Which addition checks his answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away. You should get the number you started with. 316 + 218 = 534, so the answer is right.

items.q: 397 and 402 are close. Count up to find 402 − 397.
598 and 600 are close. Count up to find 600 − 598.
Start at 245. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
Start at 316. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
Start at 478. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
Start at 587. Jump back. Where do you land?
items.e: Start at 587. Jump back 200 to 387, back 30 to 357, back 4 to 353. You land on 353. So 587 − 234 = 353.

items.q: Start at 650. Jump back. Where do you land?
items.e: Start at 650. Jump back 100 to 550, back 40 to 510, back 5 to 505. You land on 505. So 650 − 145 = 505.

items.q: The number line counts up from 380 to 500. What is 500 − 380?
items.e: Add the jumps: 20 + 100 = 120. Counting up from 380 to 500 is 120, so 500 − 380 = 120.

items.q: What is the missing jump?
items.e: From 525 to 575, only the tens change: 2 tens become 7 tens. That is 5 tens, so the jump is +50.

items.q: Which jumps show 263 + 134 on a number line?
items.e: 134 is 1 hundred, 3 tens and 4 ones. So jump +100, +30, +4: 263, 363, 393, 397.

items.q: A school has 352 boys and 325 girls. How many children are there in all?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Ones: 2 + 5 = 7. Tens: 5 + 2 = 7. Hundreds: 3 + 3 = 6. Answer: 677.

items.q: A farm has 168 hens and 225 ducks. How many birds are there in all?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 3 ones. Tens: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 1 + 2 = 3. Answer: 393.

items.q: Emma read 136 pages last month and 182 pages this month. How many pages did she read in all?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8. Tens: 3 + 8 = 11 tens. Make a hundred: 1 hundred and 1 ten. Hundreds: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Answer: 318.

items.q: A store has 457 red balloons and 236 blue balloons. How many balloons does it have?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Ones: 7 + 6 = 13 ones. Make a ten: 1 ten and 3 ones. Tens: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 4 + 2 = 6. Answer: 693.

items.q: Harper has 245 stickers. She gets 100 more. How many stickers does she have now?
items.e: Adding 100 changes only the hundreds: 2 hundreds become 3 hundreds. 245 + 100 = 345.

items.q: Jayden has 390 points in a game. He wins 10 more points. How many points does he have now?
items.e: 390 has 9 tens. 1 more ten makes 10 tens, which is 1 hundred. So 390 + 10 = 400.

items.q: A box has 486 beads. Grace uses 152 beads. How many beads are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Ones: 6 − 2 = 4. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. Hundreds: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 334. Check: 334 + 152 = 486.

items.q: A library has 725 books. Kids take home 318 books. How many books are still there?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Ones: 5 − 8? Not enough ones. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Hundreds: 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 407. Check: 407 + 318 = 725.

items.q: A bakery made 540 cookies. It sold 270 cookies. How many cookies are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Ones: 0 − 0 = 0. Tens: 4 − 7? Not enough tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 14 − 7 = 7. Hundreds: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 270. Check: 270 + 270 = 540.

items.q: A school has 300 milk cartons. Kids drink 125 at lunch. How many cartons are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Ones: 0 − 5? Not enough ones, and there are 0 tens. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens. Then trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 5 = 5. Tens: 9 − 2 = 7. Hundreds: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 175. Check: 175 + 125 = 300.

items.q: A red tower has 365 blocks. A blue tower has 142 blocks. How many more blocks does the red tower have?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. Hundreds: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 223. Check: 223 + 142 = 365.
